open_points.subject: photo_preparation public surface
open_points.question: Are both names required exported capabilities, or may the later contract combine, omit, rename or keep either one private?
options: Export only `prepare_photo` and build the publication within it
Expose one differently named operation that performs both responsibilities
open_points.default_guess: Export both named capabilities, with `prepare_photo` producing M03 and `build_publication` producing M05.

open_points.subject: photo_preparation access to the run timezone
open_points.text: - A2, rule 5 of A7, and the form of the Portal's `photo.publish` body.
open_points.question: How may `photo_preparation`, which must apply A2 rules 3 and 4, obtain the A8 `timezone` setting: by depending on the runtime-settings module or by receiving the timezone value from its caller?
options: The caller passes the validated timezone into `prepare_photo`
`photo_preparation` depends directly on the runtime-settings module or settings object
open_points.default_guess: Pass the validated timezone into `prepare_photo`, keeping runtime-settings access outside the module.

open_points.subject: photo_preparation access to A2 policy constants
open_points.text: - decoding an accepted source and the limits of A2;
open_points.question: Does `photo_preparation` import the A2 policy constants directly from their data-provider module, or does its caller supply the applicable limits and encoding values?
options: Depend directly on the data provider for all A2 constants
Receive the policy values from the caller
Receive a single policy/configuration object owned by another module
open_points.default_guess: Depend directly on the data provider for the fixed A2 policy constants.

open_points.subject: stored-image invariants INV-03 and INV-14
open_points.text: - reading a source file or writing a stored image;
open_points.question: Which module owns the persistence-side obligation that the bytes written as the stored image are exactly the metadata-free, size-checked bytes produced by `photo_preparation`, so that INV-03 and INV-14 remain true even though their declared owner must not write the image?
options: `photo_preparation` owns the invariants through an explicit output contract that the writer must preserve byte-for-byte
The stored-image writer co-owns INV-03 and INV-14
A delivery orchestration module owns the handoff from prepared bytes to storage
open_points.default_guess: Give `photo_preparation` an explicit byte-level postcondition and make the delivery/storage boundary preserve those bytes unchanged.
